content: 1. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the dose of larotrectinib by 50%. Once the CYP3A4 inhibitor has been discontinued for 3-5 half-lives, resume the prior larotrectinib dose. 2. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Do not coadminister lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 3. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Do not coadminister lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 4. Coadministration of lenacapavir with tipranavir/ritonavir may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance. The use of tipranavir/ritonavir with lenacapavir is not recommended. 5. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of letermovir by other mechanisms (see comment). Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of letermovir via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration of letermovir with P-gp inducers. 6. Tipranavir alters estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method instead. 7. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Tipranavir decreases lopinavir levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism, while lopinavir increases tipranavir levels by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives, resume the previous lorlatinib dose. 10. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of lenvatinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine due to the potential for increased toxicity. 12. Tipranavir decreases meperidine levels but increases the levels of its metabolite, normeperidine, which raises the risk of seizures. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation due to higher systemic exposure to midazolam. 14. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of neratinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of nintedanib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration, especially with P-gp inducers that are also CYP3A4 inducers. 18. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 19. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 21. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 23. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 25. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of pimozide by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. 29. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by combined CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. If unavoidable, reduce the pralsetinib dose as per prescribing information. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitors. 30. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of quazepam by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 33. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Inform patients to avoid pomegranate or grapefruit products. 34. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by other mechanisms. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. 36. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose to 10 mg twice daily with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 37. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 39. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 40. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
